fields.summary: Autonomous plan run for change set 01M75T742VGKA5XMRRXV4W6ZKP. No owner was present. The planner read the change set's intent (filed by the owner on 2026-11-11), the disk-low guard it should mirror (daemon-disk-guard, inbox-disk-low, healthDisk, RHIZA_TEST_FREE_BYTES) and the daemon settings, status and health capabilities. It raised four choices as one question for the arbiter: which intent the change set serves, the hold and release rule with defaults, how load and memory are read per platform, and when a hold reaches health and the inbox. The arbiter took every recommendation (Decision daemon-load-memory-hold-shape): serve m4-orchestrated-by-rhiza; hold when the 1-minute load per core is over rhiza.daemon.maxLoad (default 3.0) and release once the 5-minute load per core is back under it; hold while MemAvailable is under rhiza.daemon.minMemory (default 2G); 0 or empty disables each; Linux reads /proc, macOS reads load only, other platforms skip and say the reading is unavailable; daemon status and the log show every hold and release at once, health and the inbox once a hold has lasted 30 minutes, a fixed threshold. The planner then split the work into four leaves: the start hold itself, the two settings, the daemon status and log reporting, and the 30-minute health and inbox report.
